page_title: See which app is draining your MacBook, in minutes

sources.entry: WattMate - See which apps and AI coding agents are draining your MacBook battery, right from the menu bar, in real watts and the minutes you get back by quitting one. [![App Store][app-store Icon]](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6803641012)

summary.name: WattMate
summary.one_liner: A macOS menu bar app that shows which apps and AI coding agents are using battery power, in watts, and how many minutes you would get back by quitting each one.
keywords: which app is draining my mac battery
battery minutes saved by quitting app
use_cases: find which app drains a MacBook battery
estimate battery minutes gained by quitting an app
check what an AI coding agent left running
investigate battery loss overnight on a Mac
track battery health and charge sessions over months
summary.what_it_does: WattMate lives in the macOS menu bar and lists apps and terminal coding agents in real watts, grouping helper processes with their parent app. It projects how many minutes of battery quitting a given app would add, and after quitting it re-measures the Mac to show what actually changed. It logs overnight wake-ups with the app that requested them, and keeps summaries of battery sessions. It also reports battery health and, when plugged in, whether the adapter can supply enough power for the Mac's load. Graphics energy is only a total, and the Neural Engine is not attributed to any app.
notable: Shows power in watts per app and minutes gained by quitting, instead of Activity Monitor's unitless Energy Impact
Post-quit receipt re-measures the Mac 2 minutes after quitting an app to check the promised gain
Tracks AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI, and can flag processes they left running
Logs overnight wake-ups with the requesting app name
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and Apple silicon; the page says Intel support is asked about in its FAQ but the answer is not in the extracted text
Free tier of 10 days for the full app; afterwards Pro is $9.99 a year or $19 launch-price lifetime (regular $29)
Graphics energy is a total only; per-app split is approximate
Minute projections are rounded cautiously and are estimates, not guarantees
